basics.name: Kristin Boden
basics.label: AI Enablement & Adoption Leader · Digital Transformation · Fractional Head of Digital
basics.summary: Digital leader who pairs hands-on AI and automation work with 25+ years of driving technology adoption across large, change-resistant organizations. Sole technical architect of nike.com (1997) and its first e-commerce platform; led a 13-year enterprise digital transformation reaching 25,000+ users and 375+ web properties; today builds AI workflow automations and operates a DTC e-commerce business. Specializes in AI enablement and adoption, change management, train-the-trainer/champion programs, and translating complex technology into decisions non-technical leaders can act on. Open to remote roles (incl. higher education); based in the Portland, OR metro; not relocating.

work.name: (TB)oden / digital
work.position: Founder & Principal — AI Enablement, Automation & Digital Operations
work.summary: Independent practice spanning AI enablement/adoption advisory, workflow automation, program management, QA strategy, and fractional digital leadership.
highlights: Designed and deployed AI-powered operational automations end to end, including a SKU-keyed product-content pipeline (Mac Shortcuts + Hazel + AI image tagging) that classifies and routes assets automatically.
Operate a DTC resale e-commerce business sourcing-to-ledger: auction sourcing, product taxonomy, multi-channel listing, order management, and full chart-of-accounts in Zoho.
Advise on AI tool selection, workflow redesign, enablement, and change management; maintain hands-on ML fluency via Colab (summarization, tokenizers, generative models).
Serve as fractional / interim digital leader for organizations needing senior digital and AI-adoption leadership without a full-time hire.

work.name: Dia & Co (Contract via (TB)oden/digital)
work.summary: QA transformation for a DTC fashion e-commerce platform.
highlights: Stood up agile QA frameworks plus automated and visual-regression testing, reducing technical debt.
Built custom JQL dashboards (active defects, automated tests, covered requirements, defects-fixed-per-sprint) for real-time, data-driven QA.
Drove covered requirements to 100% within two months; embedded QA into dev, brand, design, and marketing workflows.

work.name: Portland State University
work.position: Director, Web Communications (Enablement & Enterprise Digital Transformation)
work.summary: Led enterprise digital strategy, standards, governance, accessibility, budget, and organization-wide technology adoption across 375+ web properties serving 25,000+ students and 5,000 faculty.
highlights: Rebuilt the entire web ecosystem into an enterprise Drupal multisite empowering non-technical content editors (earlier phases with ImageX; final Drupal 7-to-8 rebuild with Promet Source on Acquia). Publicly documented on Drupal.org with Kristin credited as PSU project lead: 340 multisites/40,000+ pages consolidated to 216; 300 authors built 200+ sites in under 3 months; 500 content editors. Released open-source; presented at Drupal business gatherings.
Drove 90.8M page views / 60.2M unique in a year; cut page load from 20+ seconds to under 1 second.

Built and directed a team of trainers delivering a train-the-trainer enablement program scaled from 318 sessions in year one to 1,500+ users/year (850% increase in offerings); recruited and coached 500+ embedded content-owner champions.
Owned the digital operations budget and vendor strategy; saved $1M+ via platform consolidation ($123K/yr software + ~$1M/yr hardware & personnel) and negotiation.

Led migrations Saga CMS to Drupal 6 to Drupal 7 to a full rebuild; owned web accessibility strategy (WCAG / Section 508) for all centrally hosted sites; led cross-functional governance with executives.
Remote-capable leadership: ran fully remote training and operations in 2020.

work.name: Nike
work.position: Technical Webmaster/Architect, nike.com → Director, Consumer Direct Digital IT
work.summary: Sole technical architect on the founding team that launched nike.com; later led the global rollout of NIKEiD.
highlights: Built nike.com from the ground up and stood up Nike's first complete e-commerce infrastructure (logistics, call center, CRM, payments, returns, content management) in under 8 weeks.
Architected for 99.9%+ uptime through massive traffic spikes; selected the (pre-IPO Akamai) CDN still in use across the nike.com ecosystem decades later.
Delivered global brand experiences: 'World Body' (Sydney 2000 Olympics — 14 locations, 8 languages), Radio Free Sydney, FZT nikefootball MMO, Nike Golf/Running, Brand Jordan.
As Director, led the global NIKEiD direct-to-consumer customization rollout and a center of excellence for Nike Retail back-end and POS systems (Nike Maxim award).
Drove organizational change by merging creative and technical teams and introducing agile methods, improving delivery timelines 60%+.

work.name: Northwest Regional Educational Laboratory (NWREL)
work.position: Internet Applications Specialist / Research Consultant / DBA / Unix Sysadmin
work.summary: Led NWREL's creative and technical web team; strategic Internet-technology consultant to education agencies.
highlights: Built some of the first web and gopher sites in the non-profit/education space, before the public '.com' era.

Moderated the 'K-12 and the Internet' panel (as Kristin Boden-MacKay, NWREL) at a FARNET conference in fall 1994, alongside internet pioneers including Mark McCahill (creator of Gopher); documented in the official Internet Monthly Report, November 1994.
Installed networks across regional school districts to support the then-new internet protocol; national presenter and writer.

work.name: Lewis & Clark College
work.summary: Statistical-analysis consultant (SPSS, SAS) and builder of early Internet web servers; honored as 'Academic Technologies, Emeritus.'
highlights: Designed instructional materials and reusable SPSS/SAS components for liberal-arts research.
Designed, coded, and maintained early Internet web servers prior to '.com'.

work.name: Riverfront Cottage
work.summary: Short-term-rental business with full P&L, operations, and values-led, award-winning hospitality.
highlights: Earned Airbnb SuperHost status every year since launch, plus Guest Favorite — 4.93/5 rating, 100% response rate, peak occupancy — with dynamic pricing and multi-OTA channel management.
Earned LGBTQ+-inclusive (Booking.com Travel Proud) and sustainability certifications across Booking.com and VRBO; extensive collection of strong guest testimonials (riverfront-cottage.com/reviews).
Proof of operator skills that transfer to digital leadership: customer-experience focus, operational consistency, and measurable, repeatable quality.
